| `ContosoApp.Core` | **8.0.0** |
| `ContosoApp.Api` | **8.0.0** |
| `ContosoApp.Services` | **8.0.1** |

The Services project references `8.0.1` while Core and Api pin `8.0.0`. Because Services also has a `ProjectReference` to Core, NuGet will resolve conflicting versions at build time. While NuGet will unify upward, this creates fragility — a future mismatch with a breaking minor version bump could cause runtime `MissingMethodException` or `FileLoadException`. The same risk applies to the test framework packages below.

---

### 🟡 Warnings

#### 2. No Central Package Management — scattered versions across all 5 projects

Every `PackageReference` carries an inline `Version`. Additionally, test packages drift between the two test projects:

| Package | Api.Tests | Core.Tests |
|---|---|---|
| `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` | **17.9.0** | **17.10.0** |
| `xunit` | **2.7.1** | **2.8.1** |
| `xunit.runner.visualstudio` | **2.5.6** | **2.8.1** |

This is a maintenance hazard. A single `Directory.Packages.props` with Central Package Management eliminates the problem entirely.

#### 3. Seven properties copy-pasted across all 5 projects

These appear identically in every `.csproj`:

```xml
<TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
<Nullable>enable</Nullable>
<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
<EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
<Company>Contoso</Company>
<Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
```

These belong in a `Directory.Build.props` at the repo root. If the team decides to target `net9.0`, they must edit 5 files instead of 1.

#### 4. `PrintBuildInfo` target duplicated in 3 source projects

The identical custom target appears in Core, Api, and Services:

```xml
<Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Message Importance="high" Text="Building $(AssemblyName) [$(Configuration)]" />
</Target>
```

This belongs in `Directory.Build.targets`. Additionally, this target has **no `Inputs`/`Outputs`**, which means it runs on every build unconditionally — acceptable for a `Message`-only target but worth noting as a pattern to avoid for targets with side effects.

#### 5. `DocumentationFile` duplicated in 3 source projects

```xml
<DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
```

This is repeated in Core, Api, and Services but absent from test projects (correctly). This should be centralized via a condition or placed in a `src/Directory.Build.props`.

---

### 🔵 Suggestions

#### 6. Dual JSON serializer dependency

- `ContosoApp.Core` uses `System.Text.Json 8.0.5`
- `ContosoApp.Services` uses `Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3`
- `ContosoApp.Api` transitively gets both

Consider standardizing on `System.Text.Json` (the modern, built-in, allocation-efficient option) unless Newtonsoft features are specifically required. Having both increases deployment size and creates two serialization code paths to maintain.

#### 7. Multiple `PropertyGroup` blocks in source projects

Core, Api, and Services each have two `<PropertyGroup>` blocks — one for general properties and one for `DocumentationFile`. These should be merged for readability (after centralization, the second block disappears entirely).

#### 8. `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions` is a transitive dependency for the API project

`ContosoApp.Api` references `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions` directly, but this is already pulled in transitively through the `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` SDK and through the `ProjectReference` to Core. The explicit reference is redundant and adds a version to maintain. Consider removing it from Api and letting it flow transitively (or rely on CPM to keep it aligned).

---

### 🟢 Positive

1. **SDK-style projects throughout** — no legacy `<Import Project="$(MSBuildToolsPath)..."` or `packages.config`. All 5 projects are modern SDK-style.
2. **`TreatWarningsAsErrors` and `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild` enabled** — excellent build discipline applied consistently.
3. **Test projects correctly set `<IsPackable>false</IsPackable>`** — prevents accidental NuGet package creation from test assemblies.

## Recommended Fix — Concrete Files to Create

### 1. Create `Directory.Build.props` (repo root)

Centralizes all shared properties. Source projects and test projects inherit automatically.

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
    <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
    <Company>Contoso</Company>
    <Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

### 2. Create `src/Directory.Build.props`

Source-only settings. Uses `<Import>` to chain to the root props.

```xml
<Project>
  <!-- Chain to repo-root Directory.Build.props -->
  <Import Project="$([MSBuild]::GetPathOfFileAbove('Directory.Build.props', '$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)../'))" />

  <PropertyGroup>
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

> **Note:** Use `<GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>` instead of manually setting `<DocumentationFile>`. The SDK computes the correct path automatically — one property, zero chance of path mismatches.

### 3. Create `Directory.Build.targets` (repo root)

Centralizes the shared custom target.

```xml
<Project>
  <!-- Only emit build info for source projects, not tests -->
  <Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build"
          Condition="!$(MSBuildProjectName.EndsWith('.Tests'))">
    <Message Importance="high" Text="Building $(AssemblyName) [$(Configuration)]" />
  </Target>
</Project>
```

### 4. Create `Directory.Packages.props` (repo root)

Enables Central Package Management and pins all versions in one place.

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- Shared packages -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions" Version="8.0.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="System.Text.Json" Version="8.0.5" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Swashbuckle.AspNetCore" Version="6.5.0" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- Test packages -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk" Version="17.10.0" />
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit" Version="2.8.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="2.8.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="NSubstitute" Version="5.1.0" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

> This unifies `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions` to `8.0.1` (highest) and all test packages to their latest versions.

### 5. Simplified project files after centralization
